title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 333 (Disclaimer of onerous property)

content.overview: The Company Liquidator may, with leave of the Tribunal and within the statutory time, disclaim onerous property of a company being wound up—land burdened with onerous covenants, shares or stocks, property not readily saleable because of onerous obligations, or unprofitable contracts. Disclaimer determines the company’s rights and liabilities in the property from the date of disclaimer without generally affecting third-party rights except as necessary to release the company.
content.glance: Liquidator may disclaim onerous land, shares, unsaleable property or unprofitable contracts with Tribunal leave within twelve months (or extended time).
content.study: Section 333 enables the Company Liquidator to free the estate from burdensome assets or contracts. The power covers land with onerous covenants, shares or stocks, property that is not saleable or readily saleable because the possessor is bound to perform an onerous act or pay money, and unprofitable contracts. Disclaimer requires Tribunal leave and must be in writing. The ordinary period is twelve months after commencement of winding up (or extended by the Tribunal); if the Liquidator only becomes aware later, the period runs from awareness. Disclaimer determines the company’s rights, interests and liabilities from the date of disclaimer, but does not affect other persons’ rights except so far as necessary to release the company.

sections.heading: Disclaimable property
sections.body: Land with onerous covenants; shares/stocks; property not readily saleable due to onerous obligations; unprofitable contracts.

sections.heading: Procedure and effect
sections.body: Written disclaimer with Tribunal leave within twelve months (or from awareness / extended time). Determines company’s rights and liabilities; limited effect on third parties.

examples.title: Unprofitable lease
examples.body: The company holds a long lease with high rent and onerous repair covenants. The Company Liquidator, with Tribunal leave, disclaims the lease within twelve months under s. 333.

hypotheticals.question: Can the Liquidator disclaim an unprofitable supply contract?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes, if it is an unprofitable contract and the Liquidator obtains Tribunal leave and acts within the statutory period.

misconceptions.trap: Disclaimer automatically extinguishes all third-party rights.
misconceptions.correction: Disclaimer affects third-party rights only so far as necessary to release the company and its property from liability.
